gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 12?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 12 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Ensemble spread remains narrow, though slight upward revisions could occur if steering patterns strengthen; traders are monitoring the next 00Z and 12Z model cycles for confirmation ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from European models indicate daytime maxima in Munich near 30–31 °C on August 13, with narrow spreads of 1–2 °C reflecting modest uncertainty in boundary-layer mixing and local advection. A broad ridge supporting subsidence and light easterly flow has sustained the warmth, while overnight radiative cooling keeps minima in the mid-teens. Historical August climatology centers on 24–25 °C highs, so the current setup represents a modest positive anomaly without extreme heatwave amplification. Trader consensus clusters on 30–31 °C because resolution hinges on the official DWD station reading, where small shifts in cloud cover or wind could tip the exact peak. Updated model runs and the final 24-hour guidance expected on August 12 remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover and widespread showers across the Tokyo region on August 12 are the dominant factors suppressing daytime heating, keeping the highest temperature centered on 27–28°C.** The Japan Meteorological Agency’s guidance explicitly forecasts a maximum near 28°C under these conditions, with extensive low-level clouds and precipitation limiting incoming solar radiation despite the seasonal background of above-normal warmth for mid-August. 

Ensemble forecast variability clusters tightly around this range because modest changes in shower timing or intensity can shift the peak by 1–2°C, while any prolonged drier breaks would be required to push readings to 29°C or higher. Historical August climatology in Tokyo shows typical highs near 31–32°C under clearer skies, but the current synoptic pattern—with its emphasis on moisture and reduced insolation—explains why traders assign the large majority of implied probability (over 89% combined) to the 27°C and 28°C outcomes. Updated model runs and official briefings through the morning of the 12th continue to reinforce this capped thermal profile.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent short-term forecast model consensus from agencies like the Japan Meteorological Agency points to partly cloudy conditions with isolated thunderstorms on August 14, moderating peak radiative heating and holding Tokyo's daily maximum near 28–29 °C. The strengthening Pacific High continues to advect warm, humid maritime air northward, sustaining urban heat-island amplification, yet increased cloud cover and potential afternoon convection are expected to cap extremes below historical mid-August averages. Ensemble guidance shows limited spread around these values, with slight downward revisions in the latest runs reflecting greater moisture and reduced insolation. Traders weigh these variables against typical climatological highs near 31 °C when assessing resolution probabilities.

These conditions favor daytime surface heating while boundary-layer moisture and minor timing differences in any weak frontal passage create the market’s clear tilt toward 30 °C (58 %) over 31 °C (30 %). Model spread remains modest, reflecting typical late-summer variability, with lower probabilities assigned to 29 °C or 32 °C tails. Updated ICON and ECMWF runs expected before evening will further constrain surface energy-balance projections ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast uncertainty for Tokyo’s August 14 maximum centers on expected cloud cover and scattered thunderstorms, which limit daytime heating and keep official readings clustered near 27–29 °C. Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble models show a narrow range around these values, with precipitation probabilities of 30–40 % during peak heating hours reducing the chance of brief clear spells that could push readings to 30 °C or higher. Urban heat island effects and humidity levels near 80% further influence observed peaks, while historical analogs from similar synoptic patterns confirm reduced highs under overcast skies. Updated model runs and JMA briefings expected in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine resolution thresholds around these values.

Ensemble model guidance shows modest spread around 27–30°C depending on exact timing of any convective bursts, consistent with trader-implied odds clustering tightly at 27–29°C. Urban heat island effects and humidity levels near 80% further influence observed peaks, while historical analogs from similar synoptic patterns confirm reduced highs under overcast skies. Updated model runs and JMA briefings expected in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine resolution thresholds around these values.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 14 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest numerical weather models and Japan Meteorological Agency guidance point to a highest temperature near 28–29°C in Tokyo on August 14, as persistent moisture and increased cloud cover moderate peak heating under the seasonal Pacific high. These conditions limit surface insolation and enhance boundary-layer mixing, keeping daytime maxima close to or slightly below the 31.5°C climatological normal while humidity sustains elevated heat indices. Ensemble spreads reflect uncertainty in exact cloud timing and any weak frontal passage, which could shift outcomes by 1–2°C, explaining the tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around the 27–29°C range rather than higher values favored in drier analogs.
